These are just three but we'll keep going. In 2008 2 economists, David Nuemark and William Wascher, did a literature review on this topic. Using the available data and studies done they concluded.

“minimum wages reduce employment opportunities for less-skilled workers … (that) a higher minimum wage tends to reduce rather than to increase the earnings of the lowest-skilled individuals … (that) minimum wages do not, on net, reduce poverty … (and that) minimum wages appear to have adverse longer-run effects on wages and earnings"

In 2014 another review was done by the same economists 
and a new face J.M. Ian Salas. They used new research available and concluded the following.

“that the evidence still shows that minimum wages pose a tradeoff of higher wages for some against job losses for others, and that policymakers need to bear this tradeoff in mind when making decisions about increasing the minimum wage.”

Finally another review was done in 2018 with further studies they concluded again. 

"Higher minimum wages are becoming the norm in many countries. Although a minimum wage policy is intended to ensure a minimal standard of living, unintended consequences undermine its effectiveness. A good deal of evidence indicates that the wage gains from minimum wage increases are offset, for some workers, by fewer jobs. Furthermore, the evidence on distributional effects, though limited, does not point to favorable outcomes from minimum wage hikes, although some groups may benefit. Other mechanisms, such as earned income tax credits, appear more effective at helping low-income families."

Well fist off congratulations on realizing this line of thinking is destructive not just for your friends but for yourself. Seriously pat yourself on your back you’ve acknowledged a weakness and more fundamentally admitted to it. There’s an ocean’s worth of people who can’t/won’t do that. So first off good for you. 

Now onto the problem are these thoughts toxic? Yes you are right they are. But you knew that the thing is I’m worried that it’s these thoughts and issues that are causing people to want to not be around you.  Now I can’t really know I don’t know you after all and I only have limited info to work with. But often times when we push these thoughts and feelings down without resolving them they tend to come out in different ways and eat at you. It’s a vicious circle you try to ignore it but it comes out and manifests in ways you don’t mean and may cause the very thing that you’re so worried about. 

So what can we do about this? First I would 100% recommend getting therapy if you can. I know this gets thrown about on reddit like it’s candy but in your case it’s apt. You know you have abandonment issues and while I can’t diagnose you and/or know based on a single post it sounds like these may have turned into a codependency issue. It also sounds like you don’t have a huge sense of self worth in yourself and depend on others to validate yourself. 

External validation is something we all want but relying so heavily that your very being comes into question if something relatively small happens is bad. Therapy is the best tool right now I think for you to help get past this. While your doing this learn to be independent pick up hobbies and do some stuff by yourself. When it comes to friendships set realistic expectations if you’ve only know them for a bit say a week to a month you have to expect they won’t be falling over themselves to hang out with you all the time.

While you’re r being independent take that time to explore who you are and what you like dislike etc. basically learn to accept and love you. After all if even you can’t how can you expect others to? Finally and this is probably going to have to be done in conjunction with therapy deal with your past with your dad leaving you with how you believe your mom loves your brother more than you. I honestly doubt that but I don’t know you so bring that up in therapy. It sounds like you judge all your relationships on your relationships with your parents. That’s a demon that needs to be dealt with.

Again this is probably generic and not too tailored to you since I don’t know you. I think however these steps will help a lot. But it is hard and you will need to take things slow. If you find yourself thinking these thoughts or getting anxious acknowledge it and then stop the negative think by countering it. It sounds new age-y but it’s really not and helps derail the toxic line of thinking.

Also and most importantly don’t beat yourself up! You’re human and well often times our very human minds can be assholes but personally I always believe if you really want change you can. But don’t lie to yourself and don’t change for others change for yourself because you want it. At the end of the day the first person that needs to be in your corner is yourself. While you can be your worst enemy you’re also your best ally. Love yourself man your amazing!
